messages:
Lena (Design): Working on the confirmation copy for 'Rollback quantization' in the model settings modal. Current copy is terse and some customers found it unclear about quality impact. Dropping a few variants for review.

Omar (Product): Please post variants. We should call out perf vs quality tradeoffs and any irreversible bits. Legal prefers 'permanently' when history is removed.

Lena (Design): Variant 1 — compact, direct:

  "Rollback quantization?"
  "This will restore the model weights to the previous (non-quantized) state. Requests may be slower and more expensive, but output quality will match the prior version. This action can be undone by re-applying quantization."
  Buttons: [Cancel] [Rollback]

Kai (Eng): Slightly misleading: rollback may drop cached optimizations and could invalidate payloads in KV cache. Also mention that rolling back triggers a restart and brief disruption.

Ritu (QA): From testing: sometimes metrics briefly spike after rollback. Suggest a heads-up about 'short period of degraded throughput' not 'slower' which is vague.

Lena (Design): Variant 2 — explicit, safety-first:

  "Revert quantized model"
  "Reverting will replace the currently deployed quantized weights with the previous full-precision variant. This will restore pre-quantization output characteristics but may cause a short deployment restart and a temporary increase in latency and cost. Any cached inference state tied to the quantized variant may be invalidated."
  Buttons: [Cancel] [Revert model]

Omar (Product): I like the clarity but 'revert' vs 'rollback' word choice — which do we prefer in our product language? We should be consistent. Also include link to docs about quantization tradeoffs.

design-bot: Note: primary destructive button pattern uses imperative phrasing and danger styling. Secondary (cancel) should be the default focused element per modal pattern.

Lena (Design): Variant 3 — safety + guidance + link:

  Heading: "Rollback quantization"
  Body: "This action restores the previous (non-quantized) model variant. Expect a brief deployment restart, temporary increases in latency, and higher per-token cost. Cached inference state tied to the quantized variant may be invalidated.

  See: "Quantization guide" (opens companion docs) for when to use rollback."
  Inline note: "If you rely on consistent latency for live traffic, consider scheduling during a maintenance window."
  Buttons: [Cancel] [Rollback quantization]

Kai (Eng): Variant 3 is my vote. For the inline note, prefer 'maintenance window or low-traffic period' and let's include a dependent count if active requests are above threshold (e.g., show a warning: 'High active traffic: consider scheduling').

Ritu (QA): Accessibility: ensure heading is announced as H2, provide aria-describedby linking to the body and the inline note, buttons have accessible names and the docs link has target=_blank with rel=noopener. Also confirm translations for 'quantized' map to the right term in locales.

Omar (Product): Approved with minor edits: use 'Rollback quantization' heading, body to include 'This action is not destructive to stored data' to reassure users that logs/metrics remain. Add a docs link text 'Learn more about quantization and rollback'.

Lena (Design): Final proposed copy for handoff:

  Heading: "Rollback quantization"
  Body (aria-describedby): "This action restores the previous (non-quantized) model variant. Expect a brief deployment restart, temporary increases in latency, and higher per-token cost. Cached inference state tied to the quantized variant may be invalidated. This action does not delete stored logs or metrics."
  Link: "Learn more about quantization and rollback"
  Inline warning (when active traffic high): "High active traffic detected (kind: warning)  Consider scheduling rollback during a low-traffic window."
  Buttons: [Cancel] [Rollback quantization]

Kai (Eng): I'll implement the dependent traffic check and warning text; will ensure modal focus order and aria attributes are in the PR. I'll also add a small telemetry event for rollbacks.

Ritu (QA): I'll add regression tests for restart behavior and confirm the warning shows when traffic > threshold. Also will validate translated strings.

Omar (Product): Thanks everyone. I'll loop in Docs and Legal for copy review and ship checklist. :white_check_mark:

Lena (Design): Filing follow-up to add a tooltip variant for the inline warning and a shorter tooltip copy for constrained screens. Thanks! :sparkles:
